title: Inspect and extend: Plan inputs, fee, change, and dust
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/wallet-core.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve utxo selection, fee estimate, amount validation, and unsigned output construction.
problem: A UTXO is an unspent piece of value. The planner selects enough pieces to cover amount plus estimated fee, then considers change and a dust threshold. Trace the UI request into buildUnsignedTransaction. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/wallet-core.ts` and the related project files: src/wallet-core.ts; src/screens/SendScreen.tsx.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to utxo selection, fee estimate, amount validation, and unsigned output construction.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: The transaction is unsigned; fee size/rate assumptions are simplified, the change output currently uses an empty placeholder address, and no real payment should be made.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A UTXO is an unspent piece of value. The planner selects enough pieces to cover amount plus estimated fee, then considers change and a dust threshold. Trace the UI request into buildUnsignedTransaction.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/wallet-core.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
